items.ladder_title: The Iran war and Pakistan as mediator

en.stem: In 2026, Iran declared which waterway closed during its war with the US and Israel?
options: The Strait of Hormuz
The Strait of Malacca
The Bosphorus
The Suez Canal

items.ladder_title: The Iran war and Pakistan as mediator

en.stem: In April 2026, US Vice President JD Vance held direct talks with Iran in which city?
options: Doha
Geneva
Islamabad
Muscat

items.ladder_title: The Iran war and Pakistan as mediator

en.stem: Pakistan carried proposals between the US and Iran and helped them agree a ceasefire, but could not impose a deal on either side. What is this role called?
options: Appeasement
Mediation
Adjudication
Arbitration

en.stem: Petrol and diesel prices in Pakistan jumped by Rs55 a litre in March 2026. What was the main reason?
options: The IMF set a new petrol price for Pakistan
Saudi Arabia stopped selling oil to Pakistan
Pakistan's main refineries shut down for repairs
War in the Middle East pushed up world oil prices

en.stem: Headline: "Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves fall sharply." Why does this worry the government?
options: It may be unable to pay for imports and debts
The State Bank must stop printing rupees
Taxes collected inside Pakistan will fall
Remittances from abroad will be blocked

en.stem: "Pakistan secured a rollover of deposits from friendly countries to shore up its foreign reserves." What does "rollover" mean here?
options: Lenders agreed to push back the repayment date
The deposits were turned into grants, not loans
Pakistan paid the deposits back ahead of time
The deposits were moved to the IMF's account

en.stem: Which group controlled Gaza before the October 2025 ceasefire?
options: The Houthis
Hamas
Fatah
Hezbollah

en.stem: What does the "two-state solution" refer to?
options: Reunifying North and South Korea
Splitting Sudan into two countries
Dividing Kashmir between Pakistan and India
An independent Palestinian state alongside Israel

en.stem: What were the Abraham Accords (2020)?
options: A defence pact among Gulf states aimed at Iran
A US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas
Arab states agreeing to normal ties with Israel
A UN plan to create an independent Palestinian state

en.stem: Pakistan hosted the 2025 Champions Trophy, but India played its matches in Dubai. What was the main reason?
options: Pakistan's new stadiums were not finished in time
Dubai offered the teams much higher prize money
India's government didn't let its team go to Pakistan
The ICC moved the matches because of extreme heat

en.stem: In 2025, India said it was holding which agreement with Pakistan "in abeyance"?
options: The Tashkent Declaration
The Indus Waters Treaty
The Liaquat-Nehru Pact
The Lahore Declaration

en.stem: Which institution brokered the Indus Waters Treaty in 1960 and has a role in its dispute process?
options: SAARC
The World Bank
The International Court of Justice
The UN Security Council

en.stem: India and Pakistan fought a short conflict in May 2025. What set it off?
options: A border clash in Sindh's Rann of Kutch
A dispute over the Kartarpur Corridor
A row over the Champions Trophy
An attack that killed tourists in Pahalgam

en.stem: In August 2019, India changed the status of Indian-administered Kashmir. What did that move do?
options: Ended its special autonomous status
Made the Line of Control the official border
Agreed to a UN-supervised plebiscite
Handed part of Ladakh to China

en.stem: Why does Pakistan usually emphasise the UN Security Council resolutions on Kashmir, while India emphasises the Simla Agreement?
options: Both documents call for Kashmir to become an independent state
Simla referred the dispute to the ICJ; the resolutions did not
The resolutions favour India's position; Simla favours Pakistan's position
The resolutions support a plebiscite; Simla commits both sides to bilateral talks

en.stem: In May 2025, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir was promoted to which rank, held before only by Ayub Khan?
options: Marshal of the Air Force
Supreme Commander
Field Marshal
General of the Army

en.stem: What happens if a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister passes in the National Assembly?
options: The Prime Minister is removed from office
Fresh general elections are held automatically
The Senate must approve it before it takes effect
The President takes over the government

en.stem: Headline: "Centre and provinces fail to agree on the next NFC Award." What does the NFC Award decide?
options: How National Assembly seats are divided among the provinces
How federal tax revenue is shared between the centre and provinces
How much Pakistan repays the IMF each year
How Indus river water is shared among the provinces

en.stem: What is the IMF?
options: A UN court that settles financial disputes between countries
An international lender that helps countries facing payment crises
The World Bank's special fund for building dams and roads
A bank owned and run by the United States government

en.stem: The IMF has pressed Pakistan to end fuel subsidies, even when oil prices rise. Why does the IMF usually ask for this?
options: To raise the profits of oil companies
To bring petrol prices down for consumers
To cut Pakistan's oil imports from the Gulf
To cut government spending and the budget deficit

en.stem: "The IMF will release the next tranche once Pakistan meets its structural benchmarks." What is a structural benchmark?
options: The interest rate charged on the IMF loan
A minimum level of foreign reserves the IMF guarantees
A ranking of Pakistan's economy against other countries
A reform step Pakistan agreed to complete

en.stem: Pakistan often asks the Afghan Taliban government to act against the TTP. What is the TTP?
options: An Afghan refugee organisation based in Pakistan
The Afghan Taliban government's own army
A Baloch separatist group fighting in Balochistan
A Pakistani militant group active inside Pakistan

en.stem: Headline: "Foreign Office summons Afghan envoy." What does this usually mean?
options: The diplomat is invited for routine trade talks
Pakistan has cut diplomatic relations with Afghanistan
The diplomat is called in to receive a formal complaint
The diplomat is being expelled from the country

en.stem: Pakistan says its strikes inside Afghanistan target militants who attack Pakistan from there. Which right under the UN Charter is Pakistan usually invoking?
options: The responsibility to protect
The right to self-determination
The right of self-defence
Collective security under Chapter VII

items.ladder_title: Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and defence pacts

en.stem: In August 2026, Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Makkah with which two countries?
options: Saudi Arabia and Turkiye
Qatar and the UAE
Saudi Arabia and Iran
China and Turkiye

items.ladder_title: Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and defence pacts

en.stem: Under that agreement, as under NATO's Article 5, an armed attack on one member is treated as an attack on all. Which principle is this?
options: Balance of power
Collective defence
Non-intervention
Self-determination

en.stem: The NPT is often in the news about Iran and North Korea. What is the NPT?
options: An alliance of countries that have nuclear weapons
A treaty that aims to stop the spread of nuclear weapons
A treaty that bans all nuclear testing
A UN body that inspects nuclear power plants

en.stem: Which statement about India, Pakistan and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) is correct?
options: Neither country has signed it
Only India has signed it
Both signed it but later withdrew
Both signed it as nuclear-weapon states

en.stem: Headline: "Pakistan reaffirms its policy of credible minimum deterrence." What is Pakistan signalling?
options: It will use nuclear weapons only if attacked with them first
It keeps the smallest nuclear arsenal of any nuclear state
It keeps enough force to deter attack, not to win a numbers race
It will match India's nuclear arsenal weapon for weapon

en.stem: Gwadar port in Balochistan is being developed mainly with investment from which country?
options: China
The United Arab Emirates
Saudi Arabia
The United States

en.stem: Headline: "New CPEC projects announced for Gwadar." Why does Gwadar matter so much to China?
options: It is China's main naval base in the Indian Ocean
It is the only warm-water port China can use
It holds large oil reserves China plans to extract
It gives China a shorter route that avoids Malacca

en.stem: Since 2023, Pakistan has sent hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants back to which country?
options: Myanmar
Iran
Afghanistan
Bangladesh

en.stem: Pakistan hosts millions of Afghan refugees. Which UN agency is mainly responsible for refugees?
options: UNICEF
UNHCR
UNESCO
WHO

en.stem: Pakistan has never signed the 1951 UN Refugee Convention. What does this mean?
options: The UN must pay all refugee costs in Pakistan
Refugees get Pakistani citizenship after ten years
It is not bound by the treaty's refugee rules
Refugees in Pakistan have no legal rights at all

en.stem: Pakistan, China, Russia, India and several Central Asian states are all members of which organisation?
options: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
SAARC
BRICS
The Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO)

en.stem: An analyst writes: "SCO membership lets Pakistan build trust with rivals and manage disputes through shared rules." Which IR theory does this reasoning reflect?
options: Liberalism
Marxism
Realism
Constructivism

en.stem: Which five countries are the permanent members of the UN Security Council?
options: USA, UK, France, Russia and Saudi Arabia
USA, UK, France, Russia and China
USA, Russia, China, India and France
USA, UK, Germany, Japan and China

en.stem: Pakistan sits on the UN Security Council for 2025-26. What kind of seat does it hold?
options: A permanent seat with a veto
An observer seat that cannot vote
A seat it holds as a nuclear power
An elected two-year seat without a veto

en.stem: "The draft resolution was adopted 13-0, with two permanent members abstaining." What happened?
options: It was adopted
It needs a second vote
It failed due to the abstentions
It goes to the General Assembly

en.stem: News reports often mention COP29, COP30 and so on. What is COP?
options: The annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank
The yearly meeting of the world's 20 largest economies
The yearly UN conference on climate change
A UN conference on refugees and migration

en.stem: After the 2022 floods, Pakistan pushed for a "loss and damage" fund at the UN climate talks. Who is mainly expected to pay into it?
options: Every UN member equally, through fees
Countries hit hardest by climate disasters
Private insurance companies
Rich countries that have emitted the most

en.stem: Under the Paris Agreement, what are NDCs?
options: Penalties for countries that miss their climate goals
Money rich countries pay to poorer countries for climate damage
Climate targets that each country sets for itself and updates over time
Emission limits that the UN sets for each country

en.stem: Who represents Pakistan at the United Nations in New York day to day?
options: Pakistan's Foreign Minister
The UN Secretary-General
Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN
Pakistan's ambassador to the United States

en.stem: A foreign diplomat in Islamabad breaks a law. Why can Pakistan usually not put them on trial?
options: Their embassy pays a fixed fine instead
They have diplomatic immunity
Pakistan's courts cannot try foreigners
Only the UN can put diplomats on trial

en.stem: "The diplomat was declared persona non grata." What does this mean?
options: The host country has ordered the diplomat to leave
The two countries have cut diplomatic relations
The diplomat has lost immunity and can now be arrested
The diplomat's own country has recalled them for consultations

en.stem: In 2026, young protesters in India began calling themselves 'cockroaches'. What first set off their protests?
options: Leaked and cancelled national exam papers
A government ban on TikTok
A sharp rise in petrol prices
A new compulsory military service law

en.stem: In September 2025, Gen Z protests in Nepal, sparked by a social media ban, led to what?
options: Parliament banned all political parties
The Prime Minister resigned
The army took over the government
Nepal's monarchy was restored

en.stem: Bangladesh's 2024 student protests, which ended Sheikh Hasina's rule, began over what?
options: A rise in electricity prices
The jailing of opposition leaders
Quotas for government jobs
Delays to the national election

en.stem: SAARC has not held a leaders' summit since 2014. What is the main reason usually given?
options: Member countries stopped paying for it
China blocked SAARC from meeting
Afghanistan withdrew from the group
Tensions between India and Pakistan

en.stem: In 2025, Pakistan's government recommended which world leader for the Nobel Peace Prize?
options: Donald Trump
Xi Jinping
Recep Tayyip Erdogan
Mohammed bin Salman

en.stem: Pakistan said it could join the international force for Gaza, but not if its mandate included one task. Which?
options: Rebuilding hospitals and schools
Disarming armed groups in Gaza
Guarding aid convoys
Training Palestinian police

en.stem: Headline: "G7 leaders meet to discuss the global economy." What is the G7?
options: The seven biggest oil-exporting countries
The UN's seven largest donor agencies
The seven countries with nuclear weapons
A group of seven large, wealthy democracies

en.stem: "Soft power" is a country's ability to:
options: Pressure others through economic sanctions and trade limits
Win wars quickly using small, highly trained forces
Damage rivals' systems through cyber attacks and hacking
Influence others through the appeal of its culture and values

en.stem: Headline: "Pakistan removed from the FATF grey list." Which countries are put on the grey list?
options: Countries with poor human-rights records
Countries suspected of exporting nuclear technology
Countries with weak anti-money-laundering controls
Countries with dangerously high government debt

en.stem: What does the "security dilemma" describe?
options: A state must choose between two allies that are rivals of each other
A state must trade off national security against human rights
One state's arms build-up makes others feel less safe, fuelling an arms race
A state must decide whether to join a military alliance

en.stem: In IR theory, what does "anarchy" mean?
options: The collapse of government inside a single country
Constant chaos and fighting between all states
Rule by militias and armed groups instead of governments
There is no world government above states to enforce rules

method: Rasch-style model on all questions + each question's own pilot answers and faculty estimate (faculty = 4 people, model = 4 people). Levels: IR/PS students = technical; others >= 50% correct = medium, else easy.
